scenes.narration: We have mapped the surface of Mars in greater detail than the floor of our own ocean. Eighty percent of the sea has never been seen by a single human being.
That is not poetry. It is a measurement. Mars is fully photographed. The ocean is a guess, drawn mostly from sound.
Sunlight dies at about one thousand meters. Below that there is no warmth, no color, and pressure high enough to crush a submarine in seconds.
And yet life is everywhere. Most deep sea creatures make their own light. On this planet, glowing is not rare. Being visible is.
So the next time someone says the frontier is in space, remember: the largest world we have is the one we live on top of, and we have barely looked.
